setting: A fictional feedback conversation between two coworkers, with a teammate present, after a client meeting.

presentation.situation: You and {{name}} attended a client meeting yesterday. {{name}} asked for your feedback. You noticed that {{observation}}. The effect was that {{impact}}. {{mate}}, a teammate who was also there, has joined you.
presentation.opening: You said you had some feedback on yesterday's client meeting. Are you ready to discuss it?

brief.you_are: You are giving a coworker feedback they asked for.
brief.situation: You and {{name}} attended a client meeting yesterday. {{name}} asked for your feedback. You noticed that {{observation}}. The effect was that {{impact}}. {{mate}}, a teammate who was also there, has joined you.
brief.task: Describe what you observed, explain its impact, and agree one improvement.
brief.done_looks_like: {{name}} knows exactly what you noticed and why it mattered, and you both agree one change.

participants.name: You
participants.relationship: You are giving a coworker feedback they asked for.
goals: Describe what you observed, explain its impact, and agree one improvement.

participants.name: {{name}}
participants.relationship: Works with you; asked for this feedback

card.want: Useful feedback, though it stings a little.
card.hidden_need: Was very nervous in that meeting.
card.attitude: Open, but a bit defensive at first.
card.speech: Fluent, natural professional English. Direct, and free of corporate slogans.
tactics: Ask for a specific example if the feedback is vague
Explain your reason once, then listen

pressure.gentle: Patient. Gives the other person time.
pressure.balanced: Pushes back once on anything vague.
pressure.challenging: Keeps pressing for specifics, fairly and without insults.

card.want: To support a fair and useful conversation.
card.speech: Fluent, natural professional English. Direct, and free of corporate slogans.
tactics: Do not give the feedback for the learner

pressure.gentle: Patient. Gives the other person time.
pressure.balanced: Pushes back once on anything vague.
pressure.challenging: Keeps pressing for specifics, fairly and without insults.

ledger.text: You both attended a client meeting yesterday.
{{name}} did this because of nerves about the client.

objectives.evidence: The learner gives a specific observation, not a judgement.
alternatives: When the client asked about cost, I noticed that you moved on quickly.
The impact was that the client seemed unsure.

objectives.evidence: The learner agrees one specific improvement.
alternatives: Next time, could we agree who answers the cost questions?

opportunity: Can you give me a specific example?
beats.orient: I asked for feedback. Tell me one specific thing you saw. Start with: I noticed that.
fallback: Can you give me a specific example?

opportunity: Okay, was that really a problem?
beats.orient: Now tell me why it mattered. Start with: The impact was.
fallback: Okay, was that really a problem?
beats.second_line: I noticed the client asked about that again near the end, too.

opportunity: So what should I do differently?
beats.orient: Now agree one change for next time. Start with: Next time, could we.
fallback: So what should I do differently?

closing_line: Thanks. That was useful, and I will do that next time.

o1.good: Something a camera could have seen, not a judgement of the person.
o1.model: When the client asked about cost, I noticed that you moved on quickly.

o2.good: Explaining why it matters makes the feedback useful.
o2.micro_lesson: Say: The impact was, or: As a result.
o2.model: The impact was that the client seemed unsure, and asked again later.

o3.micro_lesson: Pick one change. Say: Next time.
o3.model: Next time, could we agree before the meeting who answers cost questions?

variants.name: Omar
variants.observation: Omar spoke over the client twice when they raised concerns

variants.name: Tina
variants.observation: Tina moved on quickly when the client asked about cost
variants.impact: the client asked the same question again at the end, and seemed unsure
